description: Gift cards: the liability ledger store, the forward-only settlement ladder with two-leg is_fully_settled, the Wix Service Plugin JWT verifier, the two new Lambdas (wecare-gift-cards and wecare-wix-giftcard-spi), their three provisioner scripts with the customer-managed KMS key and the version-pinned cryptography layer, and six test files. Resolves HIGH-3 for the gift-card side (DECISION 5), HIGH-4 (redeem_cap defined once), HIGH-6 (DECISION 9: GCTXN# gains paymentAttemptId so GC_VOIDED is reachable), MEDIUM-4 (drop the Content-Type rejection; the three-segment check is the discriminator), MEDIUM-5 (remove the customer hold/release routes - five routes not seven) and MEDIUM-7 (rename the stale 'reference' test names). Independent of FEAT-001; ordered after it only because FEAT-003's gate edits need both to exist. Corresponds to plan.md items 12-21.
steps: Read .agents/tasks/wix-coupons-giftcards-20261001/plan.md (especially DECISIONS 5, 6, 8, 9, 10) and gift-cards-service-plugin-20261001.md sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9.1, 10 BEFORE writing code. context.json replaces re-exploration; do not re-derive what it states.

Item 12: create amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/gift_card_store.py. Partition key is HMAC-SHA256(pepper, NFKC(code).upper()).hexdigest() - NEVER the code. The pepper comes from wecare/wix/giftcard-spi -> code_pepper, referenced by id and read LAZILY at request time. Row types per section 6.3 with DECISION 9 applied: GCTXN#<codeHash>#<transactionId> gains paymentAttemptId, GCTXNID#<transactionId> points to {codeHash, paymentAttemptId}, and referenceId on GCTXN# is correlation only and never a key. The GIFTCARD# row gains the DECISION 5 attributes activeHoldAttemptId, activeHoldPaise and activeHoldExpiresAtMs. The value ceiling is the SPI's 99_999_999_999 paise, asserted on issuance AND on every credit. Define redeem_cap(*, balance_paise, wix_collection_paise) -> min(balance_paise, wix_collection_paise - RAZORPAY_MIN_LEG_PAISE) ONCE, with RAZORPAY_MIN_LEG_PAISE = 100, and have both the validator and the split call it (HIGH-4). Balance moves are a single atomic `ADD balancePaise :neg` under ConditionExpression `balancePaise >= :amount`; the GCORDER#<codeHash>#<paymentAttemptId> claim is a conditional put written BEFORE the decrement. Codes are 16 characters from a Crockford-style alphabet generated with `secrets`, never `random`. PIN comparison uses hmac.compare_digest. Logs carry codeLast4 only, rendered ****1234.

Item 13: create amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/gift_card_settlement.py, mirroring payment_status.py's construction exactly: five STRING stage values (GC_UNKNOWN, GC_NOT_REQUIRED, GC_HELD, GC_REDEEMED, GC_VOIDED) and a SEPARATE STAGE_RANK dict with GC_UNKNOWN deliberately absent so stage_rank returns 0 through .get; condition_expression(); and advance(attempts, *, attempt_id, stage, **evidence) as ONE conditional UpdateItem whose evidence keys are the CLOSED four-key set giftCardRequiredPaise, giftCardCodeHash, giftCardRedeemedPaise, giftCardTransactionId - anything else raises, and verifiedCapturedPaise is excluded on purpose because it is the Razorpay leg's evidence. advance raises StageRegressed on ConditionalCheckFailedException. Declare RAZORPAY_EVIDENCE_ATTR and RAZORPAY_VERIFIED_PAISE_ATTR as module constants so a rename decided in another session is one line. Implement is_fully_settled(attempt) per section 3.2 verbatim: the required == 0 branch is a membership test over (GC_NOT_REQUIRED, GC_UNKNOWN), the closure compares verifiedCapturedPaise + redeemed == int(attempt['amountPaise']), and the function NEVER raises on a missing attribute. Read the Razorpay leg only through payment_attempt.may_create_order. No decision compares a raw 'captured' literal.

Item 14: write tests/test_gift_card_store.py covering spec tests 42-64 with MEDIUM-7's renames applied - 49 becomes test_a_second_redeem_for_the_same_payment_attempt_returns_the_same_transaction_id, 50 becomes ..._for_the_same_payment_attempt_does_not_move_the_balance, 53 becomes test_two_different_payment_attempts_each_deduct_once. Add a test enumerating every DynamoDB access pattern and asserting exact-key-or-status-index only with zero scan (pins HIGH-3), and a test that a void carrying ONLY a transactionId resolves both the card and the attempt (pins HIGH-6 / DECISION 9). Test 46 pins the gift-card/coupon logging asymmetry from this side.

Item 15: create amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/gift_card_spi_auth.py exposing verify(raw_body, *, headers, now) -> Context. The raw request body IS the JWT. Honour isBase64Encoded FIRST, then use the three-base64url-segment check as the real discriminator. MEDIUM-4: DROP the Content-Type rejection entirely - parse the body as a JWT regardless of declared type, because the only documented plain/text example is the app-install instance-id callback and 401-ing every live call on an undocumented header value is feature-dead rather than fail-closed. Ignore Authorization entirely. Then verify the signature with cryptography (load_pem_public_key + public_key.verify, PKCS1v15 and the hash the alg names), with the algorithm allowlist {RS256, RS384, RS512} and alg:none plus every HMAC alg refused outright; aud == the configured app id with absent or multi-valued rejected; iss == 'wix.com' exact; iat <= now + 60 and exp > now - 60 with a missing claim REJECTED not defaulted; then data.metadata parsed as a Context with metadata.instanceId checked against the installed instance; then data.request returned. Parse claims with json.loads(..., parse_float=Decimal). Read the public key from wecare/wix/giftcard-spi -> public_key by id, LAZILY per request. Every failure returns 401 with an EMPTY body. No secret appears in any logging expression, not even reduced to a bool.

The brief named tests 100, 107a and 113 as xfail(strict=True). All three assert properties that hold TODAY, so a strict mark would xpass immediately - a failure under this feature's own acceptance criterion - and, worse, would switch off the only assertion that fires when the hazard arrives. This is exactly the precedent FEAT-001 set with coupon test 52a, and the reasoning is written into each test's docstring.

The design itself says the equivalent cart_v2 test "must KEEP PASSING unchanged... it is the test that proves SEAM-G1 narrowed the gate rather than opening it". Marking it would remove the detector for SEAM-G1 opening all three rails instead of one.
* Test 107a. The coupon suite already owns the general subset relation (`test_the_iam_simulation_covers_every_action_the_checkout_policy_grants`, unmarked and passing), and the design says whichever document lands second should EXTEND it rather than duplicate it. Rather than edit FEAT-001's file, this feature carries the gift-card-specific IMPLICATION as `test_the_gift_card_grant_and_its_simulation_cannot_drift_apart`: IF provision_checkout.py's policy names the GiftCardsTable THEN that ARN is in the simulated `tables` list and DeleteItem is in `_SIMULATED_ACTIONS`. Vacuous today, fires on a half-done SEAM-G9.
* Test 113 (`test_the_initiation_reserve_path_writes_no_gift_card_attribute`). Section 8.3 declares that producer out of scope and the test exists so the omission stays deliberate and VISIBLE. There is nothing pending about it; it is a gate. It `skip`s if initiation.py is absent, because that module is untracked in git.

SPEC TESTS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN, AND WHY
* tests/test_gift_card_settlement.py was NOT created. It appears in this FEAT's acceptance-criteria command line but in none of its steps, and the design puts the whole ladder (tests 65-86) in tests/test_gift_card_two_leg_finalization.py, which is where every `advance` / `stage` / `STAGE_RANK` / `condition_expression` / `is_fully_settled` assertion lives. A second file would have split one subject across two reports. The acceptance criterion says "omit any file not created".
* Spec test 57 (`"GiftCardsTable" in check_data_model_drift.UNDECLARED_ALLOWED`) is DEPENDED ON, not duplicated: section 10.2 assigns that single edit and its test to the coupon document, so one file is edited once by one session. What is asserted here instead is the part that needs no edit - `expected_table("GiftCard") == "GiftCardsTable"` and `"GiftCard" not in EXPLICIT_TABLE`.
* Spec test 91 is written as a measurable property rather than as a receipt renderer, because no receipt projection exists in this feature's owned files: it asserts the card is read from `paymentSummary.giftCards` and that `priceSummary.discount` is zero, and that `reconcile_with_wix` never references `discount` (AST).
* Spec test 98's second half is asserted as UNREACHABILITY rather than as a refusal, and the reason is arithmetic rather than laziness. Under DECISION 10 the cap is `min(balance, wixCollection - 100)` while the payable is `collection + fee + gst`, so `remainder >= fee + gst + 100` for every accepted redemption - a sub-100 remainder is unrepresentable, exactly as section 4.1 says of full cover. The explicit `GIFT_CARD_LEAVES_UNCHARGEABLE_REMAINDER` check is retained as a backstop and the test drives it with a collection exceeding the payable (a producer-bug shape), with the table as a spy asserting the hold is never taken.

FIVE IMPLEMENTATION DECISIONS NOT IN THE DESIGN, EACH LOAD-BEARING
1. `GCID#<giftCardId>` is a SEVENTH row type, not in section 6.3. `GET /gift-cards/{giftCardId}` (section 7.2) has to resolve a card by OUR id, and the only alternatives are a `Scan` or a second GSI - a GSI being eventually consistent and so unable to back a staff read of a balance that has already moved. A pointer row is the same device `GCTXNID#` already is and keeps every access exact-key. It carries `codeHash` and `codeLast4` only, so it is not a second place the code lives.
2. `activeClaimAttemptId` is a FOURTH DECISION 5 attribute beside the three named. The design requires the `/v1/redeem` refusal to be one exact-key GetItem reading `activeHoldAttemptId`, but a CLAIM (`GCORDER#`) is not a hold and never lapses. `_decrement` therefore sets `activeClaimAttemptId` AND fills `activeHoldAttemptId` through `if_not_exists`, so the stated reading remains literally true while a claim reserves unconditionally and a hold only until its expiry. `reserved_by(card, now_ms=...)` is the one reader.
3. The `GCORDER#` claim carries `settled: bool`. Written unsettled, marked settled by the decrement. Without it an `InsufficientFunds` failure would leave a permanent claim reporting a redemption that never moved money, and the claim cannot be deleted (test 60 bans it). A retry re-drives the decrement under the SAME transactionId. A replay presenting a DIFFERENT amount for the same claim key raises `REDEEM_AMOUNT_CONFLICT` rather than honouring either figure.
4. `_decrement` does NOT gate on the claim. It gates on balance and status only, because two genuinely different purchases of one card must each deduct - the design's own test 53. The `AlreadyRedeemed` refusal is a narrower rule with a different owner (the SPI handler, via `reserved_by`), and folding it into the store would make a customer's second purchase refuse.
5. The `cryptography` import in gift_card_spi_auth.py is GUARDED, and this is a packaging fact rather than a doubt about the dependency. `scripts/deploy_all_lambdas.py` packages the whole shared `lambda_utils` tree into every function that ships it, including `wecare-checkout`, which has no layers - and `tests/test_checkout_package_completeness.py::test_every_import_resolves` enforces unresolved imports as an ERROR. That test REGRESSED on the first unguarded version and is the collateral damage neither design doc enumerates. The import stays at module scope (moving it inside `verify` would make a missing layer invisible to tooling) and `verify` refuses every request with `SpiUnauthorized` when the layer is absent - fail closed, asserted by `test_a_missing_cryptography_layer_refuses_every_request_rather_than_skipping_the_check`. `ALLOWED_ALGORITHMS` now maps to hash NAMES rather than to `hashes.SHA256`, so the module still imports without the layer; `_hash_for` resolves the class per call from the allowlist, never from the token.

ONE SIGNATURE DEVIATION
`gift_card_spi_auth.verify(...)` returns a `Verified(request, context)` dataclass, not a bare `Context`. The brief's own step says both "-> Context" and "then data.request returned", which cannot both be satisfied by one return value: returning only the Context discards the SPI request and returning only the request discards `requestId` and `instanceId`. Returning both is the only shape that honours section 5.1 step 6. `verify` also takes `is_base64_encoded: bool` (API Gateway's flag is an EVENT field, not a header) and `reader`/`secret_id` so the public key is read lazily per request through an injected callable.

SEAM FACTS FEAT-004's HANDOFF DOC MUST CARRY
* SEAM-G4 / SEAM-G14 (the hold): `gift_card_store.hold(table, code_hash=..., attempt_id=..., amount_paise=..., ttl_seconds=900, clock=...)`. Call it AFTER `payment_attempt.new_payment_attempt_id()` and BEFORE the gateway. It is ONE conditional UpdateItem with the balance floor folded in, raises `GiftCardHeldByAnotherPurchase` (409 `HELD_BY_ANOTHER_PURCHASE`), `InsufficientFunds` (428) or `GiftCardDisabled`/`GiftCardExpired` (428), and re-taking your own hold is idempotent. Then `gift_card_settlement.advance(attempts, attempt_id=..., stage=GC_HELD, giftCardRequiredPaise=<paise>, giftCardCodeHash=<hex>)`.
* SEAM-G5 (the redemption): `gift_card_store.redeem(table, code_hash=..., attempt_id=..., amount_paise=..., source='OURS')` AFTER capture is verified, then `advance(..., stage=GC_REDEEMED, giftCardRedeemedPaise=..., giftCardTransactionId=outcome['transactionId'])`. `redeem` returns `{'committed': bool, 'transactionId', 'remainingBalancePaise', 'paymentAttemptId', 'amountPaise', 'source'}` and `committed` is False on a replay with the ORIGINAL id. Gate order completion on `gift_card_settlement.is_fully_settled(attempt)`, never on the Razorpay leg alone.
* SEAM-G13 is the one seam the settlement decision CANNOT work without. `is_fully_settled` returns False - never raises - when `verifiedCapturedPaise` is absent, so until `finalization.record_paid` writes it every gift-card order reads as not-settled. Read through `gift_card_settlement.RAZORPAY_VERIFIED_PAISE_ATTR` and `RAZORPAY_EVIDENCE_ATTR`, so a rename decided elsewhere is one line.
* `advance`'s evidence set is CLOSED to exactly {giftCardRequiredPaise, giftCardCodeHash, giftCardRedeemedPaise, giftCardTransactionId} and raises `EvidenceRefused` on anything else - including `verifiedCapturedPaise` and `razorpayChargedPaise`. It raises `StageRegressed` on a conditional failure; a backward move is an error to surface. `GC_UNKNOWN` is not writable.
* SEAM-G10 (the Wix pointer): `gift_card_store.bind_wix_order(table, wix_order_id=..., attempt_id=...)` at the `_stage(..., 'WIX_ORDER_CREATED', wixOrderId=...)` call. It REPORTS a second binding (`{'bound': False, ...}`) rather than overwriting the first.
* SEAM-G6 / the Wix order payload: the invariant is `Money.from_wix(order['priceSummary']['total']['amount']).paise == quote.total_payable_paise == verifiedCapturedPaise + giftCardRedeemedPaise`, the VERIFIED figures. Identical to coupons section 2.3's invariant with the gift-card term zero.
* The section 4.1 split and the section 4.2 reconciliation are both in the store and both ready to call: `split_payment(balance_paise=, wix_collection_paise=, total_payable_paise=, requested_paise=None)` returns `{giftCardRedeemPaise, payNowPaise, redeemCapPaise, wixCollectionPaise}`, and `reconcile_with_wix(cart_summary, gift_card_redeem_paise=, pay_now_paise=, quote=)` enforces all six identities and raises on any one. `redeem_cap` is defined ONCE and both callers go through it.
* SEAM-G11 is open: config/lambda-env-manifest.json needs `GIFT_CARDS_TABLE`, `WIX_GIFTCARD_SPI_SECRET`, `WIX_GIFTCARD_APP_ID` and `WIX_GIFTCARD_INSTANCE_ID`. Both handlers fall back to `gift_card_store.DEFAULT_TABLE_NAME` and `gift_card_store.SECRET_ID`, so they work without it; `app_id` and `instance_id` are read from the SECRET rather than from the environment, so only the table and secret names are manifest concerns.
* SEAM-G7(b) needs THREE edits, not one: `WIX_GIFT_CARD_TENDER = 'wix_gift_card_tender'`, adding it to `side_effect_guard.KNOWN_EFFECTS` (a frozenset validated in `claim()`, so the constant alone is not enough), and a `record_gift_card_tender` SIBLING of `record_external_payment` - the existing function hard-codes `paymentMethodName: 'Razorpay via WhatsApp'` and a `providerTransactionId`/`offlinePayment: False` shape that describes a gateway payment.
